pages.text: In the cracking coil, hydrocarbon chains break at random bonds, faster the hotter. Each product comes out best at its own temperature - the spread is roughly a bell around it. Coke (carbon) grows exponentially with heat; steam gasifies it away.
$(thing)Set$(): Coil temperature, Steam ratio.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Burner drift: the coil temperature varies by ±0.5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Coke is fouling the catalyst.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Hotter cracks faster; steam dilutes the oil.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Ethylene share: S ≈ e^(−((T − T*)/80 K)²)$(br)Propylene share: S ≈ e^(−((T − T*)/80 K)²)$(br)Coking rate: coke ∝ e^((T − 1150 K)/40 K) / (1 + 2·steam)
